hero.title: Start with the spatial question. Build the analysis around it.
hero.copy: Explore common geospatial questions—from choosing a site and identifying a coverage gap to understanding flood exposure, drainage patterns or vegetation condition. GriidAi helps connect the question to data, supported spatial analysis, human review and usable outputs.

definition.title: What is a geospatial use case?
paragraphs: A geospatial use case is a real-world question that depends on location, distance, spatial relationships, terrain, environmental conditions, networks or change over space. The answer usually requires a combination of data, GIS operations, assumptions, validation and a map or analytical output—not just a single GIS tool.

In GriidAi, the use case should remain connected to the method. The user defines the question, brings or discovers relevant data, reviews the proposed plan, approves supported analysis, validates the result and decides how the output should be used.

grid.title: Choose the question you need to answer
grid.intro: Start from the task your team recognizes. Each use case should show the question, the spatial evidence involved, the expected output, and the strongest published destination for deeper detail.

records.name: Site Selection
records.question: Which candidate locations deserve deeper review?
records.evidence: Criteria, constraints, proximity, overlays, ranked or filtered candidates when method is explicit.
records.proofTitle: Compare candidate locations with criteria your team can review
paragraphs: A site-selection use case should begin by making the decision criteria explicit: candidate locations, constraints, surrounding conditions, relevant proximity relationships, environmental or physical-risk context, and any approved scoring or weighting logic. GriidAi can then help organize the data and supported analysis into an inspectable plan rather than hiding the method inside a single AI recommendation.
sequence: Supporting context layers or user-provided business data.
Implementation plan with criteria / spatial operations.
Review of thresholds, units, assumptions and outputs.
Map and table comparing candidate evidence.

records.name: Coverage Gap Analysis
records.question: Where is service, access or facility coverage insufficient?
records.evidence: Facilities, demand/population/asset locations, distance or supported network/proximity evidence, gap map.
records.proofTitle: Find where service or access may be insufficient
paragraphs: Coverage-gap analysis compares the locations of services or facilities with the people, assets or areas they are intended to serve. The exact method can depend on straight-line distance, a supported network operation, service thresholds, population or demand layers, and the quality of the underlying data.

records.name: Flood & Coastal Risk
records.question: Which locations may be exposed under a defined flood or coastal scenario?
records.evidence: Scenario layer, terrain/elevation where relevant, asset/location overlays, exposure map/table.
records.proofTitle: Screen locations against a defined flood or coastal scenario
paragraphs: Flood and coastal screening should make the scenario visible: what hazard or water-level condition is represented, what geography and period it applies to, how it is combined with assets or locations, and what the resulting exposure layer means. GriidAi should support review of these assumptions before the output is interpreted.

records.name: Hydrology Analysis
records.question: How does water move across the terrain in this study area?
records.evidence: DEM, flow direction/accumulation, streams, basins/subbasins, derived map outputs.
records.proofTitle: Turn elevation data into terrain and drainage evidence
paragraphs: Hydrology use cases often begin with a digital elevation model and a study area. The method may derive or use terrain/hydrology operations such as fill, flow direction, flow accumulation, stream extraction or subbasin delineation depending on the supported workflow and the question being asked.
sequence: Select or obtain an elevation dataset for the AOI.
Inspect CRS, resolution, NoData and spatial coverage.
Run supported derivations and inspect intermediate outputs where useful.
Validate the stream/drainage/basin result against the use-case intent.
Export the analytical layers or continue into a downstream workflow.

records.name: Vegetation & NDVI
records.question: Where is vegetation condition higher, lower or changing across the study area?
records.evidence: Satellite imagery/bands, NDVI or related index, classified or continuous raster, summary statistics.
records.proofTitle: Use satellite imagery to examine vegetation condition
paragraphs: NDVI is a vegetation index derived from red and near-infrared reflectance. A use-case page should not stop at the formula; it should show the imagery or bands used, date/area coverage, cloud or quality constraints where relevant, the calculation, the resulting raster and the way the output is summarized or interpreted for the specific task.
sequence: Choose the study area and time period.
Use approved imagery or bring the user’s data.
Verify bands, coverage, resolution and quality constraints.
Generate and inspect the NDVI output.
Summarize or export results for the use-case context.

process.title: From a spatial question to a result you can inspect
steps: Define the business or analytical question, geography, time period and expected decision context.
Bring your own layers or discover relevant public data, then check coverage and metadata.
Translate the use case into supported spatial operations and expected outputs.
Check inputs, method, units, assumptions, validation approach and outputs before execution.
Inspect maps, tables, statistics, intermediate layers and sanity checks.
Export, communicate or continue the next analytical step. Keep the final decision with the user.

data.title: The same question can produce a different answer when the data or method changes
checks: A dataset or model may not support the entire requested area.
A historical observation, forecast, scenario and current snapshot are not interchangeable.
The level of detail can change what the analysis can support.
Distance, area and raster operations can be invalid when coordinate systems or units are mishandled.
Absence of a value is not automatically zero or “not exposed.”
A 5 km radius, 15-minute network threshold or scenario level is a user-visible assumption, not a hidden default.
Data rights affect what can be reused, exported or published.

review.title: AI can help organize the analysis. Experts still control the method and result.
moments: Input layers, geography, variables, parameters, units, method, expected output.
Intermediate layers, warnings, data checks, failed or partial steps where applicable.
Map/table/statistics, sanity checks, spatial patterns, missing data, scenario interpretation.
Method boundary, intended use, uncertainty/limitations and whether deeper expert or engineering review is required.
